fig01_thresholds: Dependence and training feasibility as the lexical threshold changes. (a) Full upstream graph, projected onto all 21,457 DAppSCAN files; the vertical axis is logarithmic. Project-only includes declared project relations; clone-only includes lexical and exact-byte relations; their joint closure forms a large component even when each relation alone has small components. (b) Eligible training among the historical DAppSCAN files for the same two 1,062-file tests. A larger file count does not imply enough positives or valid semantic independence. String-aware normalization is used; all thresholds are reported.
fig02_population: Five predeclared nested hash samples retain 10–90% of the DAppSCAN source population; 100% is the common full endpoint. The other 493 reference files remain included. Lines show median and shading shows the minimum–maximum range across the five samples, not confidence intervals. Each proportion uses the selected DAppSCAN population as denominator. These label-blind source samples differ from the historical label-informed per-project cap.
fig03_scope_ablation: Controlled scope ablation at Jaccard 0.8. A is the previously reported historical graph; B recomputes exhaustive dependencies on the same sources; C adds all upstream reference files; D also adds the external candidate. Every panel uses the same historical DAppSCAN projection or fixed test membership. Group relations are reconstructed within each population. A and B agree; the training reduction already occurs at C.
fig06_external_flow: Source-reconciliation flow for the diagnostic external cohort. Exclusions are sequential: 142 curated-source files, 16 additional paths with unresolved records, and 25 additional repeated-identity paths. The original reconciliation audit found 17 problematic paths overall, one already removed in the first stage. The final 1,998 files are a provisional source cohort, not 1,998 independently verified ground-truth cases.
fig04_representations: Factorial lexical sensitivity at Jaccard 0.8 with unchanged project and raw-identity relations. Collapsed tokens use historical identifier/number normalization; preserved tokens retain them. Masking removes explicitly declared library/interface blocks and concatenates the residual token stream; it is not verified library-origin removal or semantic analysis. All graph nodes remain. Empty representations produce no lexical shingles in all four variants. (a) Both quantities use all 21,457 DAppSCAN files as denominator. (b) Eligible, informative training files among the historical 6,587 after separation from the same 1,998-file external cohort; parentheses give reentrancy/unchecked proxy positives. External informative coverage is 1,998/1,998 for full representations and 1,995/1,998 for masked representations. These are graph and coverage results, not externally measured model performance. A separately reported segmented-mask control tests boundary-spanning shingles.
